title: The sextet and the dance dates where Louis cut loose
summary: Joe lists Trummy Young, Danny Barcelona, Billy Kyle and the bassist; concerts grew monotonous but dances let Louis play Cornet Chop Suey and Heebie-Jeebies.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Who was in the band when you joined?
Trummy Young on trombone, Danny Barcelona on drums, Irv...the bass player...
I can't think of his name. I know who you mean.
Well, we'll think of it. Billy Kyle playing piano, Louis and myself. Six pieces.
Was it near to some of the earlier New Orleans bands you'd played with or was it further away? What kind of music did Louis...?

Louis... It was a terrific band in my idea, because they was...particularly at first. Then Louis' band got kind of monotonous. Because you played the same thing every night. Except once in a while we would play a dance, and that's when you heard Louis play.
Barney never spoke about that. Neither did anybody else I've interviewed, Trummy or anybody else. I didn't know you played dances. I thought you just played concerts.

No, sir. Well, that was when we had fun, because we played such a variety of tunes. That's when old Louis would play "Cornet Chop Suey," and then "The Heebie-Jeebies" when he'd get... Old Louis...it was special when we'd play a dance and he had been hittin' that Courvoisier brandy a little -- and he'd start wailing. Then he'd half lit up, and we... I didn't never drink much, and Trummy drank a little. For instance, we had a funny arrangement on

"Twelfth Street Rag" where everybody would lay down on the floor and play. [LAUGHS] All them nuttier things on a dance. We were so glad to get away from that routine. Because when you played the concerts, everybody wanted to hear the "Blueberry Hill" and things like that. Of course, that was long before "Hello Dolly."
